entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: %s over a subquery wrapping a native-histogram-valued shape is unsupported
entries.rationale: The preceding IsPromQLRangeWindowFunc check admits only the canonical 26-name range vocabulary. lowerHistogramOrMixedCallSubqueryInput handles all fifteen SELECT/FOLD names for the histogram or mixed wideInner; histogramSubqueryFloatOnlyDropFunc handles the remaining eleven. The subqueryAnchor error paths return before this partition and do not change the function vocabulary. The added requireMixedPlanPolicy guard likewise returns before dispatch on denial, bypasses histogram-only input, and authorizes the current bespoke mixed subquery existing-plan row. It neither changes a function name nor creates a path past the exhaustive fifteen-plus-eleven split, so this trailing rejection remains unreachable.

guard: past returning if err := requirePositiveInnerRange(innerSub); err != nil
if shape := chplan.RowShapeOf(wideInner); shape == chplan.HistogramRowShape || shape == chplan.MixedRowShape
past returning if err := requireMixedPlanPolicy(wideInner, mixedSubqueryFamily); err != nil
past returning if node, matched, err := lowerHistogramOrMixedCallSubqueryInput(wideInner, shape, call.Func.Name, sub, innerSub, step, s, ctx); matched

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: %s does not accept a subquery argument
entries.rationale: lowerSubqueryOverCall is the only caller and dispatches here only after its own range-window vocabulary gate has admitted the call, so chplan.IsPromQLRangeWindowFunc has already answered true for the same canonicalised name by the time this check runs
